text: For an RDS major upgrade the parameter group for the new family (postgres16) has to exist before engine_version changes. Create it in the same apply with create_before_destroy; the old group can't be deleted while the instance still uses it.
Prod: keep apply_immediately = false and let allow_major_version_upgrade run in the maintenance window. Only staging applies immediately.
Plan/apply from your laptop: `terragrunt run-all plan` in live/<env>, then apply. Post in #infra before applying prod.
All applies go through Atlantis: open the PR, comment `atlantis plan -d live/staging/rds`, get an approval, then `atlantis apply`. Local applies are blocked by the SCP on the deploy role.

Check extensions before a major Postgres upgrade: pg_stat_statements and postgis need `ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE` afterwards, and the RDS pre-upgrade check fails on old pgaudit versions. `SELECT * FROM pg_extension;` on a replica first.
Terraform state is in the stratus-tfstate S3 bucket with the tf-locks DynamoDB table for locking.
Locking is S3-native now (use_lockfile = true, Terraform 1.9); the tf-locks DynamoDB table was deleted. A plan stuck on a lock means a stale .tflock object in the bucket.

Take a manual snapshot before any major upgrade: `aws rds create-db-snapshot --db-instance-identifier stratus-prod-pg --db-snapshot-identifier pre-pg16-$(date +%F)`. You can't downgrade in place, rollback means restoring from that snapshot.
Changing instance_types on an EKS node group forces replacement. Bump the launch template version instead and roll nodes with update_config max_unavailable = 1.
Staging uses single_nat_gateway = true; a NAT gateway per AZ was costing ~$100/month each.
terraform fmt and tflint run in pre-commit (`pre-commit run -a`). The aws ruleset version in .tflint.hcl is pinned, bump it on purpose and fix the new findings in the same PR.
Module docs are hand-written in each module's README.md.
Module READMEs are generated: `terraform-docs markdown table --output-file README.md modules/rds` fills the block between the BEGIN_TF_DOCS markers. CI fails when variables.tf and the README drift.
Blue/green would make the pg16 upgrade near zero-downtime but the rds module doesn't support it yet. Decision: in-place upgrade with a 20-30 min window, revisit blue/green for pg17.
No inline IAM policies. Everything goes through modules/iam-policies with the JSON in policies/; Access Analyzer runs weekly.
App DNS records under *.apps zones are managed by external-dns in the cluster, not Terraform. Don't add aws_route53_record for them.
Pehle staging upgrade karo aur app team ko 2 din testing ke liye do. Prod window Sunday 02:00 IST fixed hai, uske liye change request Jira mein pehle se daalna padta hai.
PR titles: `<env|module>: summary`. One env per PR for live/ changes so Atlantis locks don't block everyone else.
RDS FreeStorageSpace alarm lives in modules/monitoring at 10%. Prod storage autoscaling max_allocated_storage is 1000 GB.
Har resource pe cost_center tag chahiye Cost Explorer ke liye. Woh provider ke default_tags mein already set hai, resource pe alag se mat daalo warna plan mein diff aata rahega.
ElastiCache in modules/cache uses a redis7 parameter group family; changing the family recreates the cluster.
engine_version is set per env in live/<env>/rds/terragrunt.hcl inputs. The module default only applies to new instances, so don't change the module default as part of an upgrade.
No bastion anymore: `aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id>` and for databases use the AWS-StartPortForwardingSessionToRemoteHost document to forward a local port to the RDS endpoint.
